title: [observability] an open unverified_landings alert keeps its count and text current (alert.updated: the same alert, its text and evidence as the count is now)
prompt:
Spawn, mission 4, objective 219 [observability] (after 135; the lead's item of 2026-11-18 14:2x and YES on rev-b's scope, sync/obj-219/scope.md; author rev-b; readers rev-h first, rev-k second): an open unverified_landings alert keeps its count and text current.

The problem. 135's alert fires once with the count of its first reading ("10 landed objectives unverified for over a day: spawn verify list names them"). While it is open, every later reading only sees that one is open and returns, so its text and evidence stay at that count while more landings grow old or get verified. On 11-14 it said 10 while 13 or more were over a day (rev-i, 11-17). The alert records allowed fired, cleared and judged only: nothing could change an open alert.

What changes:
- A control record `alert.updated` {type, key, kind, subject, text, evidence}, written through `spawn_alert_record` (owner only). It is refused, writing nothing, unless the key's alert is open (not a notice, not cleared), of that kind and subject, and the text is not empty. The control fold sets that row's `text` and `evidence` only: its fire (fired_event_id, fired_at_ms), state and verdict are unchanged; a refold of the log gives the same row. `spawn alert record` (the CLI, 172) still takes fired or cleared only.
- The loop (crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs): Event::Update. At a reading with the unverified_landings alert open, when the reading's `old` or `newest_old_ms` differs from the open alert's evidence (`old`, `newest_landed_ms`), it records one alert.updated: the current text ("<n> landed objective(s) unverified for over <bound>: spawn verify list names it/them") and the current evidence (old, unverified, unverified_ms, newest_landed_ms, listed_since_ms, reading_ms, and fired_old, the count it fired at). A reading that finds the same records nothing. A loop started again reads the evidence back from the table, so it records nothing until the count moves. An update is not a fire: one open at a time still holds, and nothing new is notified. Clearing and the next fire are as in 135.
- Only unverified_landings writes it here. The fire's evidence is unchanged (135.sh reads it).

What stays: the read (`unverified_landings`, 135's polled SELECT) at the same cadence; no new polled read, column or index; 135.sh passes.

Files: crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (spawn_alert_record's check, the control fold), crates/spawn-postgres/src/alerts.rs (docs), crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs (Event::Update, the record path, `unverified`), crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts/guardrails.rs (its test helpers' Event arms); tests in crates/spawn-postgres/tests/alerts.rs and alerts.rs's unit tests. Owner: rsi/scenarios/219.sh, rsi/backlog/219.json.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/219.sh, black box (a real loop and serve on a scratch database, SPAWN_ALERT_UNVERIFIED_SECS=10, read through GET /api/alerts and the control log):
  (1) objective 7 old: one alert, "1 landed objective unverified for over 10 s: spawn verify list names it";
  (2) objective 10's fail after its pass makes a second old one: the same alert (its key and fired time, open, the only one) says "2 landed objectives … names them", evidence old 2, fired_old 1;
  (3) objective 7 passes: the same alert says "1 landed objective …", old 1;
  (4) readings with the same count write nothing: exactly 2 alert.updated records for its key, and one alert.fired;
  (4b) (R2, rev-k's F1) the same count with a newer old landing: objective 12 (landed N-30 s, passed) fails and objective 10 passes, both written in one transaction (spawn_verification_record twice inside begin/commit), so no reading sees one without the other: the same alert still says "1 landed objective …" (old 1, fired_old 1), and its newest_landed_ms moves from N-60 s to N-30 s;
  (5) objective 12 passes: it clears (cleared evidence old 0).
On main (7d348cfc), 219.sh exits 1 at (2): the text stays at 1.

Tests: spawn-postgres tests/alerts.rs an_open_alert_is_updated_in_place_and_nothing_else_is (the update, the refusals: another kind, no text, a key never fired, a notice, a cleared alert; refold); alerts.rs an_open_unverified_alert_says_the_count_as_it_is_now (up, the same count with a newer landing, down to the singular, no change says nothing, a restarted monitor, the clear). landed_objectives_unverified_over_the_bound_alert_once_and_clear_when_verified now says no other alert fires while one is open (its update is checked by the new test). No test is renamed or dropped.

Verified by: after landing, while an unverified_landings alert is open on live, its text in Needs you (or `spawn alerts --once`) says the count `spawn verify list` gives, within a reading of a change (the lead's or rev-b's look).
